_comment: EXPERIMENTAL. Procedural table for Logs -- per procedural_generation_scope_proposal.md #2 this was flagged 'poor fit' (bodyText IS the entry, ~80-90% prose), but the task asked to try it anyway. lib/proceduralGenerators.js slot-fills {name}/{location}/{item}/{faction} from this world's OWN live roster (lib/roster.js) wherever one exists, falling back to the generic pools below only when a world genuinely has nothing yet to reference (e.g. Logs generated before any NPCs/Locations/Items exist) -- this is the one category where grounding in real archived content, not just table variety, is the whole point.

Audio.value:
[RECORDING BEGINS -- QUALITY DEGRADED]

...still there? Okay. Okay, if anyone finds this -- {name} said {item} would still be at {location}, and they were wrong, or somebody beat us to it. Either way I'm not going back for a second look.

[LONG PAUSE]

If this is {faction} picking this up -- I want it on record I didn't take anything that wasn't already abandoned.

[RECORDING ENDS]

[AUDIO LOG -- PERSONAL]

Day whatever. Lost count again. {name} still hasn't come back from {location}, and I keep telling myself that doesn't mean what it probably means.

[SOUND OF SOMETHING SHIFTING]

Going to go looking in the morning. If someone finds this instead of me -- tell {name} I kept the {item} safe, like I said I would.

[RECORDING ENDS]

[AUDIO LOG -- FIELD REPORT]

This is {name}, reporting in from {location}. {faction} activity is heavier here than the last briefing suggested -- recommend nobody comes through alone.

[STATIC]

Also recovered a {item} on site. Flagging it for anyone who actually knows what to do with it, because I sure don't.

[RECORDING ENDS]

[RECORDING -- SOURCE UNKNOWN]

...if you're hearing this, {location} isn't safe anymore. {name} tried to warn people and nobody listened, so I'm trying again.

[PAUSE]

Whatever you do, don't go looking for the {item}. It's not worth whatever's guarding it now.

[RECORDING ENDS]

[AUDIO LOG]

Funny thing about {location} -- everyone talks about it like it's cursed, but {name} lived there for years before things went bad. Found their {item} still sitting exactly where they left it.

[LONG SILENCE]

Makes you wonder what actually chased them out.

[RECORDING ENDS]

[AUDIO LOG -- {faction} INTERNAL]

This is for {faction} eyes only. {name} confirmed the situation at {location} is worse than reported -- recommend reassigning anyone stationed there before the next supply run.

[PAUSE]

The {item} recovered from the site is being held pending review. That's all for now.

[RECORDING ENDS]

Journal.value:
Still can't sleep. Keep thinking about what {name} said before they left for {location} -- that it wasn't as bad as everyone made it sound. I hope they were right.

Found the {item} in their things today. Not sure what to do with it yet. Feels wrong to use it. Feels worse to just leave it.

Third entry this week, which is more than I usually manage. {location} is finally starting to feel less like a temporary stop and more like somewhere we're actually staying.

{name} thinks I'm being naive about it. Maybe. Traded half our {item} stock today for something we actually needed, so at least that went well.

Today {name} asked me straight out whether I trusted {faction}. Took me longer to answer than it should have.

Spent the rest of the day going through what's left at {location}, trying to figure out what's worth carrying and what isn't. Kept the {item}. Couldn't tell you exactly why.

Woke up before everyone else again. Walked out to {location} alone, which {name} would absolutely lecture me about if they knew.

Found a {item} half-buried near where the old road used to be. Didn't touch it. Some things you leave exactly where they are.

{name} left today. Didn't say much, just took the {item} and headed for {location} without waiting to see if anyone wanted to come.

I keep telling myself they'll be back. I've told myself that before about other people.

Good day, for once. {faction} came through on what they promised, and {location} is finally starting to feel secure enough to actually plan around.

{name} even cracked a joke for the first time in longer than I can remember. Small things.

Terminal.value:
> SYSTEM RECOVERY -- PARTIAL LOG RECONSTRUCTED

> {name}: requesting status update on {location} perimeter.
> SYSTEM: no response received from field unit in 6+ cycles.
> {name}: escalating to {faction}. attaching last known asset report: {item}, last logged as secure.

> [REMAINDER OF LOG CORRUPTED]

> USER {name} LOGGED IN
> NOTE: found {item} while clearing debris at {location}. logging for records, unclear if still functional.
> NOTE: {faction} contact says they want it examined before anyone else touches it.
> USER {name} LOGGED OUT

> [NO FURTHER ACTIVITY ON THIS TERMINAL]

> {name}: anyone still monitoring this terminal?
> {name}: if so, {location} needs resupply before the week's out.
> {name}: also logging the {item} we found here, in case it matters to {faction} later.

> [NO REPLY LOGGED]

contextTemplates.value: Recovered from a damaged data drive, partially corrupted.
Found tucked into a personal effects bag, water-damaged but legible.
Pulled from a terminal that shouldn't still have power.
Left behind in plain sight, like whoever wrote it wanted it found.
Recovered from a sealed container, deliberately hidden rather than lost.
Found among a scattered pile of similar entries, the rest unrecoverable.

fallbackNames.value: a scavenger who never gave a name
someone who signed only with initials

designNotes.value: EXPERIMENTAL -- rolled procedurally from a Mad-Libs template, slot-filled with real roster names/locations/items where this world had any archived yet. This is the proposal's own flagged 'poor fit': bodyText IS the entry, and a templated found-text log reads noticeably more mechanical on a close read than an AI-drafted one, even with real names slotted in. Treat this as a placeholder worth a manual rewrite, not a finished log.
